**Finding: compliant** (Section 15.2 Assignment; Change of Control, ¶¶ p0608–p0615, read with § 12.2(a)(ii) at p0489).

Why no redline:

- **Our assignment rights meet the preferred position.** Sanofi may assign to any Affiliate without RevMed's consent, and may assign the Agreement in whole, without consent, to a successor/purchaser in a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction — the full affiliate plus M&A carve-out.
- **The restriction is asymmetric in our favour.** RevMed needs our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments, and under 15.2(b) may not assign or transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent.
- **No vendor right triggers on our change of control.** RevMed's termination rights (material breach, insolvency, Sanofi Competing Product, cessation of activity) contain no change-of-control trigger, and there is no re-pricing or rights-reduction on a Sanofi Change of Control during the term — so we are clear of the walk-away scenario.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: RevMed can assign in whole on its own Change of Control without our consent (short of the preferred consent/no-competitor formulation, but mitigated by its notice obligation, our termination/alternative option on a RevMed Change of Control, and the Acquiror Family firewall conditions — at or above the mutual-successor fallback); and the post-termination royalty to us ending on a Sanofi Change of Control plus the 9.7(a) withholding gross-up allocation, which are sub-elements of separate financial terms.
